text:
Maria K: Heads up — I hit a 404 on an anchor in the runbook for Dedicated onboarding: /handbook/runbooks/dedicated#capacity-planning. Staging preview, not prod.
Lee: ugh, thanks for the catch. can you paste the exact link?
Maria K: sure: https://internal.redwood.com/handbook/runbooks/dedicated#capacity-planning — clicking the TOC entry jumps to top of page instead of anchor.
Alex P: probably changed the heading id during the last edit. who owns that doc atm? @docs-owners?
Samir: I’ll take a look, looks small. quick grep shows the heading is now "Capacity & scaling" instead of "Capacity planning" so anchor changed.
Lee: if it's just the anchor we can add a redirect anchor or tweak the toc link. which is less invasive?
Samir: redirect anchor is fine. i'll open a tiny PR: replace the TOC link with the new fragment and add an explicit HTML anchor above the heading.
Samir: PR: https://git.internal.redwood.com/docs/handbook/pull/1423 — tiny change, includes screenshot before/after.
Alex P: nice. can someone do a quick review? @Maria K can you smoke-test the staging preview?
Maria K: yea i'll check once CI finishes.
Chris: also, while we're here, should we add the runbook to codeowners? noticed it's not claimed and a few of these drift issues keep popping up.
Samir: agree — adding a CODEOWNERS entry in the handbook dir is a follow-up. will add in the PR description and mark as a separate commit.
docs-bot: automated link-checker: found 1 broken anchor in /handbook/runbooks/dedicated (detected 2025-06-01T14:12:03Z).
Maria K: CI passed, staging preview shows anchor fixed. LGTM from me.
Alex P: quick review done, left one comment about the anchor HTML comment. otherwise LGTM.
Samir: addressed Alex's comment and pushed. squashed.
Chris: thanks — can someone cherry-pick to main (we're about to run a canary deploy that pulls docs from main)?
Samir: done, cherry-picked to main and updated the PR title.
Maria K: thanks all :tada:
Lee: leaving a note in the runbook changelog too so we remember why the anchor exists.
Alex P: perfect. closing the loop — ping me if it resurfaces.
